front: What is an intraoral scanner (IOS)?
back: A device that captures direct optical impressions of the dental arches.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: What do intraoral scanners project onto the teeth to scan them?
back: A light source, either laser or, more recently, structured light.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: What are implant scanbodies?
back: Cylinders screwed onto implants so the scanner can capture implant position.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: What is a conventional physical impression, compared with an optical one?
back: An impression made with trays and impression materials.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: Name a patient-comfort advantage of optical impressions.
back: They avoid the discomfort of conventional impression materials and trays.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: How do optical impressions affect working time?
back: They are time-efficient and reduce working time and cost compared with conventional impressions.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: How fast can the latest intraoral scanners capture a full arch?
back: In less than 3 minutes.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: Which complex cases can intraoral scanning simplify?
back: Cases with multiple implants or severe undercuts.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: What step does an optical impression let the clinic skip?
back: Making a physical impression and pouring a gypsum model.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: How can a technician check a scan's quality right away?
back: The dentist can email the scan immediately and the technician can check it in real time.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: What is one of the most frequent problems with intraoral scans?
back: Detecting deep margin lines on prepared teeth, or margins when there is bleeding.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: Who may find intraoral scanners harder to adopt?
back: Clinicians with less experience or interest in technology; there is a learning curve.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: About how much does an intraoral scanner cost, per the 2017 review?
back: Roughly 15,000 to 35,000 euros depending on the model.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: How do optical impressions help patient communication?
back: Patients feel more involved in their treatment.

source.ref: Mangano F et al. Intraoral scanners in dentistry: a review of the current literature. BMC Oral Health 2017 (open access)

front: What is the most common file format for 3D files sent to a printer slicer?
back: STL.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What geometry must an STL file have to print successfully?
back: A closed geometry, not an open mesh.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What happens to the design data once a CAD design is completed?
back: It is transferred to CAM software that controls the production unit.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What can be measured on 3D models in digital dentistry before treatment?
back: Volumes and distances, for example to analyze a tooth preparation.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why do milled implant components often fit better than milled tooth-borne restorations?
back: Implant component geometry has a simple, accurate numerical representation, reducing reliance on scanning.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What are the conventional fabrication steps that CAD/CAM can replace?
back: Impression, stone model, wax pattern, investing, and replacing the pattern with permanent material.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why can conventional fabrication introduce error?
back: Much human handling and materials with processing shrinkage or expansion.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Which high-strength ceramics can only be produced by computer-aided manufacturing?
back: Alumina and zirconia.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Name material groups modern CAD/CAM machines can use.
back: Metals, ceramics, and resins.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Name metals used in CAD/CAM prosthodontics.
back: Base metal alloys and titanium.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What was the early use of CAM in prosthodontics?
back: Fixed prostheses luted to teeth.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Name two ways CAD/CAM can produce removable partial denture frameworks.
back: Directly from metal, or as a resin pattern that is cast conventionally.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Which materials can be processed by subtractive milling?
back: Metals, ceramics, resins, and waxes.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What durability advantage comes from milling from an industrial blank?
back: It relies on the manufacturer's tight quality control and reduces flaws like porosity.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Where were glass ceramics acceptable before CAD/CAM high-strength ceramics?
back: Inlays, onlays, or anterior crowns cemented with resin.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What are known limitations of zirconia?
back: A high incidence of veneer porcelain fracture and material instability.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why should zirconia be produced at accurate dimensions?
back: To avoid manual adjustment after sintering, which can cause phase transformation and defects.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: How does zirconia durability compare with metal prostheses?
back: Less durable than metal but within a clinically acceptable range.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What marginal gap is considered clinically acceptable?
back: Within 100 micrometers.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why is no tool compensation needed in additive manufacturing?
back: No drilling or cutting tool is involved.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What features can additive manufacturing reproduce that milling struggles with?
back: Detailed morphology, sharp corners, undercuts, and voids.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What is stereolithography primarily used for in dentistry?
back: Producing surgical implant guides.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Name an advantage of additive over subtractive manufacturing for large items.
back: There is little restriction on fabricating large workpieces such as facial prostheses.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What does build orientation in the slicer affect?
back: Print time, trueness, how many parts fit on the plate, and the risk of detachment.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Which orientation angle is most accurate in most studies when supports are used?
back: 45 degrees to the build plate.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Which orientation is fastest to print?
back: 0 degrees, because it needs the fewest layers.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Which orientation fits the most parts on one build plate?
back: 90 degrees.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Which orientation has the lowest failure rate from warping?
back: 45 degrees.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is warping in 3D printing?
back: The object detaching from the build plate during printing.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What do printing resins actually resemble in composition?
back: Direct or machinable composite resins, not PMMA as often claimed.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What light wavelengths activate printing resin photoinitiators?
back: UV wavelengths from 365 to 405 nm, depending on the printer.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What happens if a resin's filler content is too high?
back: Light diffuses more and the resin may no longer be printable.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Is it acceptable to use a printing resin outside its indication?
back: No. Each resin must be used within its indication; other uses are not legally compliant.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What two properties must surgical guide resins have?
back: Biocompatibility and the ability to be autoclaved.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Name dental items printing resins are offered for.
back: Models, surgical guides, aligners, splints, custom trays, crowns, and dentures.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is the main advantage of additive manufacturing in dentistry?
back: Customized devices in less time at lower cost.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is subtractive manufacturing?
back: Milling a workpiece from a larger blank with a computer numeric controlled (CNC) machine.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What does CAM software compute for a milling machine?
back: The tool path: sequencing, tools, and tool motion direction and magnitude.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why do dental mills combine burs of different sizes?
back: Because dental restoration features are uneven.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: How accurate is mill tool positioning reported to be?
back: Within 10 micrometers.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What does cutter diameter compensation in CAM ensure?
back: That the bur reaches the desired surface without removing needed material.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Which milling systems are most common in dentistry?
back: 3-axis systems.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What is an advantage of 3-axis milling?
back: Minimal calculation and shorter milling time.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What limitation do 3-axis mills have?
back: They cannot produce large prostheses.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What does the fourth axis add to a mill?
back: Blank movement in another axis, useful for large blanks and long-span frameworks.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What does the fifth axis add?
back: A rotating path of the tool or blank for complex geometry and smooth surfaces.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What is hard machining used for?
back: Metal, densely sintered zirconia, and composite resin.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What is soft machining used for?
back: Presintered zirconia.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why is presintered zirconia milled oversized?
back: It shrinks during the sintering that follows milling.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why must a hard machining mill be very strong?
back: It mills very hard blanks with heavy cutting forces.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What is additive manufacturing?
back: Joining materials layer upon layer from 3D model data.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: How many layers per millimeter do additive systems lay down?
back: 5 to 20 layers.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Name the additive systems used in dentistry.
back: Stereolithography, selective laser sintering or melting, and 3D printing.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: How does selective laser melting build a part?
back: A laser fuses metal powder layer by layer.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: How does stereolithography build a part?
back: A UV light beam cures a liquid polymer layer by layer as the platform lowers.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What finishing follows stereolithography?
back: Rinsing with solvent and curing in a UV oven.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Why is additive manufacturing more economical in material?
back: There is little waste and unused material can be reused.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: What flaw do selective laser melted metal parts show?
back: Microporosities.

source.ref: Abduo J, Lyons K, Bennamoun M. Trends in Computer-Aided Manufacturing in Prosthodontics: A Review of the Available Streams. Int J Dent 2014 (open access)

front: Name the three vat photopolymerization technologies.
back: SLA, DLP, and LCD (also called mSLA).

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What does the build plate do between layers in vat printing?
back: It lifts vertically by a few tens of microns, the layer thickness.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What happens to print time if layer thickness goes from 100 to 50 microns?
back: The number of layers and the print time double.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What light source does SLA use?
back: A high-energy laser that draws each cross-section.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why do SLA print times grow with more or larger objects?
back: The laser must cross the whole surface of each layer.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is the main difference between DLP and SLA?
back: The light source: DLP uses a projector with a chip of micromirrors.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why is DLP layer time the same regardless of how many objects print?
back: The whole layer is projected at once.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What light source does an LCD (mSLA) printer use?
back: An LED projector behind an LCD screen.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What does slicer software do?
back: Turns a 3D file into a sequence of 2D layers and lets the user set parameters and supports.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why are the first 10 to 15 layers overexposed?
back: To make the print adhere well to the build plate.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What file does the slicer generate for the printer?
back: A G-code file with the manufacturing path.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why can't a printed part be used straight off the printer?
back: The resin is not fully polymerized, so properties are unsatisfactory.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: List the post-processing steps for vat-printed parts.
back: Rinse, dry, post-cure, remove supports, and optionally polish.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What solvent is generally used to rinse printed parts?
back: 99% isopropyl alcohol.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What happens if a printed part is poorly rinsed?
back: Leftover resin fuses to it during post-curing and can affect fit.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: How long does rinsing typically take?
back: Between 5 and 20 minutes depending on the resin.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: How is a rinsed part dried?
back: With an air syringe, then left a few minutes for alcohol to evaporate.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why must each resin be cured in its recommended device?
back: Wavelength incompatibility prevents complete polymerization.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why do some makers post-cure under vacuum or nitrogen?
back: Oxygen inhibits polymerization of the surface layer.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What are breakaway supports?
back: Supports removed with simple finger pressure.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why should IPA rinsing be done under a fume hood or ventilated area?
back: IPA evaporates and is highly flammable.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is a wash unit?
back: A device that agitates the solvent to clean printed parts.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: May saturated IPA be poured into wastewater?
back: No. It is harmful to the environment and legally prohibited.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: How can usable alcohol be recovered from saturated IPA?
back: By decanting after the resin settles out.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is the main limitation of LCD printers?
back: Overheating of the LCD screen.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Why might a resin from one brand not print on another brand's printer?
back: Their light wavelengths may not be compatible.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Does FDA clear or approve printing materials alone?
back: No. FDA evaluates a material within a medical product and its intended use.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What must a practitioner printing intraoral prostheses declare to regulators?
back: That they are a manufacturer of prostheses.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: Is model printing subject to the prosthesis manufacturer obligation?
back: No, models are not affected.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What system must a producer of custom devices set up?
back: A quality control and traceability system.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What printing setups does the review recommend avoiding?
back: Uncertified printing chains and unapproved printing profiles.

source.ref: Caussin E et al. Vat Photopolymerization 3D Printing in Dentistry: A Comprehensive Review of Actual Popular Technologies. Materials 2024 (open access)

front: What is a 510(k)?
back: A premarket submission showing a device is substantially equivalent to a legally marketed device.

source.ref: FDA: Premarket Notification 510(k)

front: What is a predicate device?
back: The legally marketed device to which substantial equivalence is claimed.

source.ref: FDA: Premarket Notification 510(k)

front: How long does FDA usually take for a substantial equivalence decision?
back: Within about 90 days.

source.ref: FDA: Premarket Notification 510(k)

front: Since October 1, 2023, how must most 510(k)s be submitted?
back: Electronically using eSTAR.

source.ref: FDA: Premarket Notification 510(k)

front: Can a device be marketed before FDA finds it substantially equivalent?
back: No.

source.ref: FDA: Premarket Notification 510(k)

front: How many FDA device classes are there, and what decides the class?
back: Three, based on risk to the patient or user.

source.ref: FDA: Classify Your Medical Device

front: Which device class has the greatest risk?
back: Class III.

source.ref: FDA: Classify Your Medical Device

front: What are General Controls?
back: Baseline FD&C Act requirements that apply to all device classes.

source.ref: FDA: Classify Your Medical Device

front: When did FDA's Quality Management System Regulation take effect?
back: February 2, 2026.
